evidence: DeepSeek uses `if p1 + p2 > T` followed by `total1 > T` and `total2 > T`; GPT uses the same tests with `elif sum1 > T`; GLM does `p1 + p2 > T` and then falls through to `LOAD 2`.
affordance_in_statement: “JOB i ... cannot possibly finish by the deadline due to its own sequential stage requirements” and “LOAD c ... the total volume of work for stage c exceeds the deadline.”
removal_suggestion: Do not state the two certificate types as a complete set of direct lower bounds. Instead, describe the required certificate through a prescribed timing scenario and require the solver to derive which bound applies, while retaining the same JOB/LOAD output format and examples.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Checks each job's isolated two-stage duration, then the two aggregate machine loads.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: “JOB i” is justified by the job's sequential requirements, while “LOAD c” is justified by total serial work on stage c.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Computes `p1 + p2`, `sum1`, and `sum2`, relying on the guarantee to select the first applicable category.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: “Exactly one of the following reasons will always apply.”

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Uses the same isolated-job test followed by total stage-1 and stage-2 work tests.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The statement explicitly defines JOB and LOAD certificates using individual sequential work and aggregate stage load.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Records the first job with `p1 + p2 > T`, otherwise reports LOAD 1 or falls through to LOAD 2.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The exhaustive certificate bullets make the two sums sufficient to certify impossibility.

common_affordance: The statement exposes an exhaustive set of additive necessary conditions: an isolated job needs p1+p2 time, while a stage needs the sum of its processing times.
recommended_edit: Replace the explicit JOB/LOAD lower-bound descriptions with an indirect, scenario-based certificate definition that requires deriving the relevant timing obstruction rather than directly testing p1+p2 and the two stage sums.
